judged.message: `isSafeOriginChange` currently treats any URL string matching `^https?:` as safe, even if it changes origin. That means inputs like `https://evil.com/...` or `http://attacker.com/...` will now be accepted whenever an origin is provided, which appears to reintroduce the SSRF/open-redirect case the change is trying to prevent.

`isSafeNavigationMigrationCall()` only checks `ast.receiver` for a `PropertyRead`, but the migrated marker is emitted as a `Call` with the marker in the callee position. For expressions like `$safeNavigationMigration(foo?.bar)` this guard may not recognize the existing wrapper in all AST shapes (for example when wrapped in `ASTWithSource` or parenthesized by the parser), so the migration can still recurse into and potentially rewrite already-migrated expressions.

Removing the `unregisterTool` call means tool registrations may persist after the injector is destroyed in runtimes/polyfills that do not treat `abortCtrl.abort()` as an implicit unregister. The previous implementation explicitly cleaned up the registration, so this change can leak stale tools or leave duplicate registrations on re-creation.

`futureVersion` was bumped to 2300, but the new recommendations are keyed at 2200. This means the v22 guidance will not be treated as the current future-version guidance and can break filtering/selection logic in the update guide.

`op.attributes` is now populated with a pooled constant expression, but `serializeAttributes()` can produce non-literal expression forms that are only safe if every downstream consumer of `ProjectionOp.attributes` treats them as a generic `Expression`. This change widens the type in `create.ts`/`instruction.ts`, but it would be easy to miss a remaining call site that still assumes a `LiteralArrayExpr` and mutates or pattern-matches it as such. Can you confirm all projection consumers handle pooled constants correctly?

With `unmatchedInputBehavior: 'undefinedIfStale'`, this only tracks keys seen in `data` for the current outlet instance. If the outlet is destroyed and later recreated while reusing the same component type, previously bound inputs are forgotten, so a missing route key will no longer be cleared to `undefined` even though the component may still be carrying a stale value from its own initial state or prior reuse. Was the intent to scope this to the active component instance rather than the outlet, and if not, the seen-key state likely needs to survive outlet recreation or be tied to the component ref lifecycle instead.

`current` now includes all non-derived sources from `batch.current`, not just sources that are absent from `this.current`. This changes the meaning of the earlier `others` computation and may cause batches to be re-run for sources that were already present in the earlier batch, potentially reintroducing work that the previous filter intentionally excluded. Was the goal to widen the merge condition here?

`context.state.analysis.module.scope.declarations` is only populated when `node.metadata.can_hoist` is true. If a top-level snippet is not hoistable for any reason, its name will never be recorded in module scope, so later duplicate checks against other top-level declarations/snippets may miss it.

`parse_statement_at` now treats any Acorn error whose `pos` equals `source.length` as `unexpected_eof`, but that also catches real syntax errors discovered at end-of-input (for example an unterminated initializer or incomplete destructuring). This can mask the original parse error and report the wrong diagnostic.

Could this EOF case also need to handle a lone '/' that appears inside contexts other than tag expressions? Advancing `i` avoids the hang here, but it would be worth confirming that this branch is only reachable when skipping a non-comment slash at end-of-input, so we don't accidentally mask another malformed-input case.

`find_regex_end()` can now return `Infinity`, but this line still adds `'/'.length` before checking for that sentinel. As a result, a regex literal with no closing `/` before newline can produce `Infinity + 1`, which is still `Infinity`, so the subsequent `end === Infinity` check never runs and the scanner may skip incorrectly. This looks like it will break bracket matching around unterminated regexes.

This override forces `function_depth` to match the current fragment scope for every declaration tag. That fixes the new validator case, but can it also mask legitimate `state_referenced_locally` warnings for declarations nested inside a declaration tag expression that intentionally introduce a deeper function boundary?

When `next.type` is `undefined` but the element already has a `type` attribute, this block calls `set_attribute(..., undefined, ...)` to remove it before the main loop runs. Was that intended for all `input` updates with a spread `value`/`__value`? If not, this may briefly clear `type` on existing inputs that are being updated rather than created.

This test covers the `'a=ab&a=c' -> 'a=abc'` case, but the fix description also mentions duplicate params collapsing to the same concatenated text in the opposite direction. Was the intent to add a corresponding regression test where the previous joined string and the new joined string match but the duplicate list changes in another way?

`render_browser_table` now hard-codes Internet Explorer as `not supported`, but it still unconditionally includes the row for every target. That changes the generated output from a minimum-version table to a mixed table of supported browsers plus a special-case unsupported browser, which may be intentional, but it also means the function no longer filters unsupported rows the way it does for undefined versions. If the goal is just to document IE11, consider moving this into the docs markdown instead of the generated baseline table.

The generated feature table now links feature names to docs pages, but the `$state.snapshot` and `bind:devicePixelContentBoxSize` anchors assume those headings exist exactly as written in the companion svelte.dev PR. Could you confirm those anchor targets are stable? If the headings differ, these links will be broken in the published docs.

`destroy_effect()` now mutates `effect.f` directly instead of calling `set_signal_status(effect, DESTROYING)`. If `set_signal_status` performs any side effects beyond flipping the bit (for example, updating dependent queues or derived state), this change can leave the effect in an inconsistent teardown state.

This function now hoists the shared template itself and returns an identifier, but the old callers were removed by construction. Could any other call sites still expect `transform_template(...)` to return an expression rather than a hoisted `Identifier`? If so, they will generate invalid code or double-hoist. It would be safer to make the new return type explicit in the signature or to rename the helper to reflect the new behavior.

`ImportGlobOptionsWithoutAs` removes `as`, but the subsequent `options` parameter still accepts `ImportGlobOptions<Eager, As, BaseQueryType>` in the deprecated overload. Because `query` is now a generic parameter defaulting to `BaseQueryType`, a caller can still pass a known `query` value and a matching `as` value and potentially get the new query overload picked first. Please double-check that this overload ordering and constraint set cannot produce ambiguous or unintentionally widened inference.

This new predicate no longer matches `candidate === '/'` for non-root paths, because `base.startsWith('//')` is false and `base === '/'` is also false for any nested path. As a result, `getCommonBase()` can stop returning `/` as the shared base when that is the only common ancestor, which may break glob resolution for paths in different top-level directories.

`transform` on the OXC test plugin only rewrites identifiers, but it relies on matching the optimized dep id substring `@vitejs_test-dep-class-field-sourcemap-oxc.js`. In Vite's dep optimizer, the emitted file name is typically derived from the package id and may not preserve this exact substring once the dep is pre-bundled, so this hook may never run and the sourcemap test will give a false sense of coverage. Could this match be widened or derived from the resolved optimized file name instead?

Parsing `.map` with `JSON.parse` is done inside the same `Promise.all` as reading the JS file, and any JSON parse failure is silently treated as if no map exists. If the optimizer writes a malformed map or a partial file is observed during a race, Vite will now serve unmapped optimized deps without any signal, making the sourcemap regression hard to diagnose. Consider handling malformed maps separately and surfacing a warning or retrying when the map is present but invalid.

Merging `getEnvs(`${prefix}*`)` into `env` unconditionally can silently override values that were already loaded from `.env*` files or `process.env`. In particular, Vite currently prioritizes inline/runtime env sources in a specific order, and this blanket assignment may change that precedence for prefixed variables when Vite Task returns a value for the same key.

Setting `process.env.NODE_ENV` during config resolution changes a process-global value based on task-provided state. Because `resolveConfig()` can be called more than once in the same process (for example, for nested tools or tests), this may leak a cached NODE_ENV into later invocations and alter mode-sensitive behavior unexpectedly.

Calling `ignoreInput(outDir)` only for the top-level output directory may not cover nested paths that `emptyDir()` reads or deletes recursively. If Vite Task tracks the child entries individually, the read/write overlap check could still fire during recursive cleanup.

`setupHmrWsOptionCompat` replaces `serverConfig.ws` with a fresh object and copies values from `server.hmr`, which means an explicitly provided `server.ws = false` is discarded if `server.hmr` is also present. That makes it impossible to intentionally disable WebSocket setup while still carrying legacy HMR options through the merge path.

In `mergeConfigRecursively`, the special handling for `rootPath === 'server.hmr'` redefines `merged[key]` from `defaults` for every ws key. If `defaults` does not already contain one of these properties, `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(defaults, key)!` will be `undefined` and the non-null assertion hides a runtime crash. This path can be hit when merging partially specified configs.

Calling `setupHmrWsOptionCompat(_server)` inside `resolveServerOptions` mutates the raw server config before the resolved config is finalized. Because the compat layer installs accessors on `hmr`, later code that expects `server.hmr` to remain a plain object can observe proxy-like behavior, which may break plugins or tests that inspect or clone the config after resolution.

This test only removes `tmpBase` in `afterEach`, but `resolveConfig()` can create additional directories/files outside that subtree if it resolves a parent package or uses a different cache path than expected. Because the comment relies on avoiding ancestor `package.json` discovery, it may still be sensitive to the host temp directory layout and leave behind artifacts if the assertion fails before cleanup. Could this use `fs.mkdtempSync` for a unique per-test root or explicitly clean up the exact resolved cache directory as well?

The new `fs.existsSync(nodeModulesDir)` check treats any existing path named `node_modules` as a directory target, but it doesn't verify that the path is actually a directory. If a file or broken symlink named `node_modules` exists under the root, `cacheDir` will be set to `<root>/node_modules/.vite`, which is invalid. Consider checking `stat`/`isDirectory()` before preferring this location.

The new `glob` branch adds every match from `globSync(dep.glob)` to `deps`, but that call uses the glob's default relative/non-absolute output while the second call uses absolute paths. If downstream code expects normalized absolute paths (as the other dependency types do), this can produce inconsistent watch entries or missed invalidations when the glob resolves through different cwd/alias contexts.

This test is named 'throw an error if it contains `"` or `\'` or `\\`', but the implementation only logs a warning and leaves `allowedHosts` unchanged. The assertion also checks `warnFn` rather than an exception. Was the test name copied from an older behavior? Renaming it to reflect the warning/skip behavior would make the expected contract clearer.

`process.versions.pnp` is not a Yarn-specific signal; any runtime or shim that populates this field will trigger the warning. That can produce false positives in non-Yarn environments or tests/tooling that emulate PnP. Consider checking for Yarn specifically (or otherwise validating the package manager) before warning.

When an additional source is configured for an element that already has built-in asset sources (for example `img` or `meta`), the new code runs the default and additional `filter` functions independently, but it also evaluates the additional `srcAttributes` against the same node without merging attribute lists. That means users cannot override or extend the default set in a single entry; they can only add parallel matches. If the intent is true merging, should the lists and filter semantics be combined into one matcher per element so existing defaults and custom attributes are processed consistently?

The PowerShell command interpolates `inputPath` directly inside single quotes. If the resolved path contains an apostrophe, `GetFile('...')` will fail or parse incorrectly, causing the short-name probe to return `undefined` even when the file exists. This makes the new 8.3 coverage flaky on paths like `C:\Users\O'Brien\...` and on any future fixture with `'` in its name.

This PowerShell command interpolates `inputPath` directly into a single-quoted string. If the resolved path ever contains an apostrophe, the command breaks (and a crafted path could potentially alter the command). Since this helper is used to derive a test fixture name, it would be safer to avoid shell interpolation entirely or escape single quotes before embedding the path.

Rejecting any normalized path that contains `~` will also block legitimate filenames and directories on Windows, not just 8.3 short names. If the intent is to stop short-name bypasses, this check may be too broad and could break serving of valid assets whose names include a tilde.

The colon check now rejects every Windows path segment containing `:`, including some otherwise valid path-like inputs after the drive prefix. Because the code only strips the drive letter, a path such as `C:/foo/bar:baz.txt` will be blocked even if it is not an ADS access pattern. Is that broader rejection intentional?

This PowerShell command interpolates `inputPath` directly into a single-quoted script string. If the path ever contains a single quote, the command can fail or be interpreted incorrectly. Escaping the argument before embedding it would make the helper more robust on Windows CI.

Removing the `analyzedModules.add(i)` pre-marking means the recursive call no longer skips already-seen chunks before the lookup. If `bundle[i]` is missing, the new early return will silently treat that edge as an external module and stop traversal, which may omit transitive modules that should still be collected for the current chunk graph.

This new require path points to `./utils/code-path-utils`, but the helper was added under `lib/rules/utils/code-path-utils.js` and this file lives in `lib/rules/`, so the relative path is correct only if the file is present there. However, the diff shows the helper under `lib/rules/utils/`, meaning the import should resolve from the rule file to that location; please verify the path is correct across all rule files because a mismatch here will throw on load.

The shared helper import is newly introduced here; if the relative path does not exactly match the new utility file location, the rule will fail to load when ESLint initializes it. This should be checked against the repository layout before landing.
This rule now depends on the new shared helper module. A wrong relative path would cause a hard runtime failure for the rule, so the import path needs verification before merging.

This added require must resolve to the new utility module. If the path is off by one directory, ESLint will crash when loading this rule. Please confirm the module location and adjust the path if needed.
Like the other rules, this import now has a hard dependency on the new utility file. A bad relative path would break the rule at startup, so this needs to be validated against the actual file layout.

Adding a top-level `workspaces` field changes how `npm install` resolves the repo. In a monorepo, this can cause root installs to start hoisting/linking packages differently and may break existing CI or local workflows if the repository was not already configured as an npm workspace. Was this intended to be a repo-wide package-management change rather than just a test-runner convenience?

This config now includes `../../types`, but the deleted `packages/eslint-config-eslint/types/nodejs.d.ts` file was the only file in that folder. If the package still relies on ambient declarations from that file, the new test config will silently stop type-checking them, which can hide regressions. Please verify that deleting the old `types` entrypoint is intentional and that the new `tests/types` suite covers the same surface area.

The new shared `tsconfig.types.json` is now used for the root type tests, but the previous config explicitly listed `../../../lib/types/index.d.ts` in `files`. Switching to `include` broadens what gets picked up and can also stop guaranteeing that the intended declaration entrypoint is the one being tested. If the goal is to test a specific public type surface, consider preserving an explicit `files` entry for the main declaration file.

`process.kill(process.pid, result.signal)` re-sends the child’s signal to the current process, but this occurs only after `spawn.sync()` has already returned. That can make the wrapper exit via signal even when the child was merely interrupted, and it bypasses the explicit `process.exitCode` path entirely. Is that the intended behavior for `eslint --init/--mcp`, or should the wrapper translate signal exits into a numeric exit code instead?

The new signal test stubs `spawn.sync()` to return `{ signal: "SIGTERM" }`, but on Windows the implementation falls back to a nonzero exit code rather than an actual signal. Do we want this test to assert platform-specific behavior explicitly so it doesn’t hide regressions in the non-Windows signal path?

The new early-return condition rejects every async callback with a line break between `function` and `(`, including cases where the break is only whitespace/comment trivia. That is broader than the invalid-autofix case described in the PR and can suppress safe fixes.

`escapeDotLabelText()` is only used for `segment.internal.nodes`, but this DOT generator also emits other string values in the same output. If any of those values can contain `\` or `"` (for example, future node/edge labels derived from source text), the DOT will still become invalid. Could this helper be applied consistently to every quoted DOT field in this file?

The overload set for `CodePath.traverseSegments()` appears incomplete: the runtime API supports `traverseSegments(options, callback, thisArg?)`, but the new declarations only expose the 1- and 2-argument forms. This will still reject valid code that passes a custom `thisArg` and undermines the goal of matching the runtime API.

`globalIgnores()` no longer excludes `build/**`, but this pattern is not obviously covered by `.gitignore` in the diff. If `build/` isn't ignored by `includeIgnoreFile()`, ESLint will start traversing generated build output again.
`coverage/**` was removed from the explicit ignore list. Unless `.gitignore` already ignores coverage output, ESLint may begin linting coverage artifacts and produce noisy failures.

`mutatingExpressions.length === 1` only reports when the sequence contains exactly one counter-modifying subexpression. That means a sequence like `(j++, i--)` or `(i--, j++, k++)` is handled, but any sequence with more than one counter write is silently ignored even when one write is clearly the wrong direction and the others are unrelated. If the rule is meant to catch the direction of the actual loop counter update, this broad skip may reintroduce false negatives beyond the original comma-operator bug.

Initializing `_exportObj` with `{ __proto__: null }` fixes the prototype pollution issue for the spread/export-star path, but it also changes the object’s prototype semantics for every namespace export object. If any later code assumes a normal `Object.prototype` (for example, `hasOwnProperty` or `instanceof Object` checks), this will break those consumers. Is the rest of the SystemJS pipeline guaranteed to only treat `_exportObj` as a plain property bag?

`dynamicRequireTargets` is now set to `undefined` when `buildStandalone` is false. If the Rollup config type or plugin expects an array here, this may be treated differently from omitting the option entirely and could break non-standalone builds or trigger validation warnings.

In non-`IS_PUBLISH` builds this now unconditionally allocates and fills a `Uint32Array` for every parse, even when `options.locations` is `false`. Previously the `packed` path avoided the `fill(0xFFFFFFFF)` cost for this mode, so removing the branch may introduce an avoidable regression in the default no-loc case.

`empathic/package`'s `up()` uses `last` as the stop boundary, but the previous code stopped at `root` while also searching from `inputFileDir`. Can you confirm `last: root` preserves the old traversal semantics for all relative input paths? If `root` can be a file path or missing, the search may now walk farther than intended or stop too early.

`find-cache-directory` accepted an options object with a `name` property, while `empathic/package`'s `cache()` here is called with a bare string. If the new API expects a different shape or normalizes names differently, cache directories could change unexpectedly across platforms or package names.

`ref! ?? t.cloneNode(innerBinding)` does not preserve the old fallback semantics. The non-null assertion is erased at runtime, so if `ref` is `undefined` this expression still evaluates to the right-hand side, but the `!` makes the code look like `ref` is guaranteed and can mask downstream assumptions. More importantly, if `innerBinding` is also absent in a future path, `classRefForDefine` will become invalid and later `.name` access will fail. Can we keep the explicit nullish fallback without the assertion?

The `ReplaceSupersOptions` type was widened to allow both `objectRef` and `getObjectRef` (and likewise for `superRef`/`getSuperRef`) to be present simultaneously. If the implementation assumes these are mutually exclusive, this weakens the contract and can hide bugs where the wrong source is used. Was the exclusivity intentionally removed, or should this remain a discriminated union?

`decoratorPath` is now typed as `NodePath<t.Decorator | null> | null`. Is the `| null` inside `NodePath` intentional? If `path.get(...)` never produces a nullable node wrapper, this may be compensating for a typing issue rather than a real runtime case.

`--allowlist` now uses a required value (`<allowlist>`), which changes the previous `--whitelist [whitelist]` behavior. The old CLI accepted the flag with no value and treated it as a no-op; this new parser will hard-fail instead. If that backwards compatibility is intentional, the docs should call it out explicitly; otherwise the option parser should preserve the optional-argument behavior.

The new package accepts `module` in `--output-type`, but the underlying `buildExternalHelpers` API may not support it in the Babel version this package targets. If `module` is unsupported, this will produce invalid output or fail at runtime. Please verify the allowed values match the implementation in `@babel/core`, or reject unsupported values here before calling into the API.

This fixture is named `--output-type global`, but the arguments only set `--allowlist nonexistent` and never exercise the output-type behavior. As written, the test does not verify the new default/explicit `global` path for the extracted CLI.

`withTopicBindingContext()` now always resets `seenTopicReference` to `false` on entry and restores the previous value on exit. If this helper can be nested, an inner pipeline body that uses `#` will not be visible to the outer body once the inner callback unwinds, which changes the old "mark current context as used" behavior and can affect validation of topic usage in surrounding parses.

`nodeFsAsync` is now declared as a zero-arg arrow function that returns a template expression, but the shared `Builders`/`Pieces` contract now expects `nodeFsAsync(file: File)`. This looks inconsistent with the new helper API and could break callers that rely on the `file` argument being available for helper injection.

The new top-level-await error path now uses `file.buildCodeFrameError(specifier, ...)` instead of `path.buildCodeFrameError(...)`. `buildCodeFrameError` is usually called on a `NodePath`/AST path, not on `File`, so this may throw a type/runtime error before the intended diagnostic is produced.

`GLOBAL_TYPES.get(scope)!` assumes every scope has already been registered in the WeakMap. If `isGlobalType` is called before registration, this will throw immediately instead of treating the type as unknown and issuing the warning. That looks like a real runtime regression under strict-null checks.

`setSourcePosition(line, column)` is called after appending unmapped spaces, but it restores the source position to the start of the original whitespace span rather than its end. If subsequent mapped output relies on the current source position advancing with the generated column, this can cause later mappings to point at the wrong original location after any preserved-format spacing run.

The `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE` fallback was removed, but Node 13/older async-module error behavior is still mentioned in the surrounding comment. In environments that still surface `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE` instead of `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`, this now rethrows instead of retrying the async import path, so config loading can fail for TLA-enabled modules that used to work.

After emitting catch-up spaces with `ignoreMapping: true`, the code updates `_sourcePosition` to the target location without also advancing the generated position. If later code relies on source-position state being consistent with what was just appended, this can leave the generator in a mismatched state and produce incorrect mappings for subsequent tokens, especially across multiple catch-up segments.

The new deprecation path makes `safe=None` the implicit default, which means callers that explicitly pass `safe=None` will now silently get `safe=False` behavior rather than the previous `TypeError`/validation failure. If `None` is a possible user input here, this changes the API contract in a non-obvious way.

`hasattr(self.UserModel._default_manager, "get_by_natural_key")` is too weak to detect whether the manager actually defines a usable natural key for the user model. Many managers inherit a default implementation, so this check can still call `get_by_natural_key()` even when the model doesn't support username-based natural keys, or skip validation for managers that intentionally override lookup behavior. This makes the uniqueness bypass brittle.

This test model defines `is_superuser` but omits `is_staff`, which is normally required by `createsuperuser`/admin user semantics and by many custom user managers. Was the omission intentional? If the goal is to cover a realistic swappable user model, adding `is_staff` and setting it in `create_superuser()` would better match the code path exercised in production.

`format_debug_sql()` now unconditionally calls `sqlparse.format()`. If a backend depends on this hook but does not have `sqlparse` available or wants to return unformatted SQL, this will raise or force a dependency on the formatter. Was the intent to make this hook optional via a no-op default in the base class?

`printErrorList()` no longer formats `sql_debug` before writing it. The existing output can now span multiple lines only if the caller already preformatted it, which changes the runner’s error display behavior and may break the intended single-block formatting for debug SQL in test failures.

`_set_auth_user()` now always replaces `request.auser` with a new zero-arg async function. Is it intentional that any existing `request.auser` implementation, including wrappers that may carry request-specific behavior or caching, is discarded on login/logout?

`do_checksum()` now requires `dist_path`, but its body still uses `dist_path` from an outer scope that no longer exists. As written, any call will raise `NameError` unless a global `dist_path` happens to be defined. This breaks checksum generation for the release script.

`get_commit_hash()` is called before `build_artifacts()`. If the build step or any later pre-release operation updates the working tree or HEAD (for example via generated files, submodules, or a release workflow that tags/rewrites during the run), the recorded commit hash may no longer correspond to the artifacts you package. Would it be safer to compute the hash after the build/sanity-check sequence, or explicitly from a known release tag ref?

Could `min_itemsize` also be accepted as a sequence or other mapping-like object in this code path? The new guard only checks `isinstance(min_itemsize, dict)`, so any non-dict mapping would still fall through to the old opaque errors. Is that intentional?

The expected result for `bdate_range(end=end, periods=3, freq="3B")` does not match the semantics described in the PR. For `end='2026-03-20'`, the last on-offset business day is already 2026-03-20, so stepping backward by 3 business days should produce `2026-03-12, 2026-03-17, 2026-03-20` only if the stride is anchored differently than the code comment says. For the other parametrized ends, this expected value is also suspicious because it is reused unchanged across Fri/Sat/Sun ends even though the anchor date changes. Please verify the expected dates against the intended anchor and adjust the assertion so the test actually covers the regression.

`_set_attr_if_changed` only compares `current == value` and skips the write when that is truthy. For PyTables attributes, different on-disk representations can compare equal in Python (for example, NumPy scalar/array vs Python scalar, or dtype/encoding differences), so this optimization can leave the stored metadata in the wrong form even though it is semantically equal. That is risky for `kind`, `meta`, and `dtype` attributes that downstream readers may expect in a specific serialized representation.

This adds a full `len({len(row) for row in data})` scan before taking the fast path. For very large lists of arrays, that is an extra O(n) pass over the input and may partially offset the benefit of the optimization. Is that acceptable here, or could the check be folded into the existing iteration to avoid traversing `data` twice?

`calc_cov` now returns `NaN` whenever `nobs <= ddof`. With the default `ddof=1`, a window containing exactly one valid pair will therefore produce `NaN`, but the new regression test (`test_rolling_cov_corr_degenerate`) expects `0.0` for the last covariance value in a window with a single non-null observation. Was the intent to preserve the previous behavior of returning zero in this degenerate case?

`_subestimator_support_warnings` is only initialized on freshly created root contexts. If `get_context_path(self)[0]` returns an existing root context in a nested propagation path, this attribute may be missing and `propagate_callback_context` will raise an `AttributeError` the first time it tries to check the set.

`GridSearchCV(scoring=...)` does not typically accept a list of metric names by itself; multi-metric scoring usually needs a dict or a callable returning a dict, and `refit` must match one of those keys. As written, this example may fail or behave differently across versions.

Can we verify that the generated sphinx-gallery anchor is actually `sphx_glr_auto_examples_callbacks_plot_scoring_monitor.py`? If the gallery builds the example under a different slug or section name, this cross-reference will become broken.

`make_classification` is asked to generate 10 classes with the default `n_clusters_per_class=2`, which violates the generator's constraint that `n_informative` must be large enough for `n_classes * n_clusters_per_class`. This example will raise a `ValueError` as written.

The snippet imports and uses `sparse_interface`, but the surrounding text describes a new config key. If the actual API name is different (for example, if the config key is `transform_output`/`sparse_output` or similar in the released version), this example will be misleading or broken. Can you confirm that `sparse_interface` is the intended public keyword?

Wrapping `inspect.getmembers(self)` in a blanket `FutureWarning` filter suppresses every FutureWarning raised while introspecting the estimator, not just warnings from deprecated fitted attributes. If another property or descriptor emits a FutureWarning during repr generation, it will now be silently hidden as well.

The new early return treats any NumPy/NumPy comparison as compatible as long as both namespaces are NumPy, but the comment only justifies two specific cases. This can mask genuine mismatches where `X` and the fitted attribute are both NumPy-backed yet should still be compared on device/representation details (for example, if one side is a sparse NumPy array-like wrapper with different semantics). Consider narrowing the guard to the explicit combinations you intend to allow instead of all NumPy/NumPy cases.

Could the new `X_device is None` branch also need to handle `sp.csr_array`/other sparse array types explicitly? The message currently keys off `sp.issparse(X)`, which covers sparse matrices, but sparse arrays may present differently and may not get the intended user-facing message.
